messages:
marie: Heads up — found a surprising behaviour in the new JS SDK with project-scoped keys. If REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY is missing, it silently falls back to an org key and proceeds. This lets requests succeed but bypasses project-level quotas.

ashok: yikes. can you paste a tiny repro? env vars, snippet, and what you expected vs saw

marie: repro below:

```js
// env: REDWOOD_API_KEY=org_key  (no REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY)
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const res = await client.generate('hello');
console.log(res.meta); // shows project_id: null, billed_to: org:acme
```

expected: SDK should error when project-scoped key required or at least warn; not silently use org key and bill org

sam: FWIW Go SDK returns 400 when project key missing in this flow. so that's an SDK parity bug. probably regression from the recent auth-refactor.

olivia: quick idea: add a strict mode flag REDWOOD_ALLOW_ORG_FALLBACK=false by default + a warning log when fallback happens. also unit test to ensure behavior. we should discourage falling back for project-scoped routes.

marie: i'll open a PR today: add env var, warning, and tests. will tag @eng-ml for review and @devex for SDK parity followup. :thumbsup:

marie: yup, will add to the issue and ping billing ops
